purpose: Test whether a deterministic pre-solve router can improve AC optimal-power-flow reliability or time without changing the objective, constraints, or feasibility standard.
claim_boundary: This is an IEEE reference-network benchmark. It is not field validation, a utility deployment, a realized-savings study, or evidence that a heuristic beats the mathematical optimum.

environment.solver_family: pandapower.runopp using the PYPOWER AC OPF implementation

buswise_load_stress.description: Apply seeded active- and reactive-load multipliers while preserving each bus power factor.

connected_n_minus_one.description: Remove one in-service branch only when the resulting topology remains connected; record excluded islanding outages separately.

split_rule: Generate scenario records from the fixed seed, sort by SHA-256 of the canonical scenario specification, assign the first one-third to development and the remaining two-thirds to the locked holdout, and never tune on holdout outputs.

baselines.description: Full AC OPF with flat initialization and no router.
Full AC OPF initialized from a power-flow solution and no router.
The single initialization route selected using development results and then frozen.

candidate.description: A deterministic pre-solve router trained only on development scenarios. It may choose flat initialization, power-flow initialization, or a declared retry sequence using only pre-solve network descriptors.
forbidden_features: scenario identifiers used as lookup keys

timing_protocol.scope: Include all preprocessing, routing, failed attempts, and retries in candidate time.

statistical_plan.multiple_network_summary: Report every network and scenario family separately before any macro average.

failure_rules: A lower reported cost is not a win unless the candidate satisfies the identical objective and constraints and an independent feasibility check passes.
A speed result is not a win if failed attempts or retries are omitted from elapsed time.
An aggregate win is blocked by a guardrail failure on any reference network.
A post-hoc router designed from locked-holdout outcomes is exploratory and requires a new prospective holdout.
